title: Keywords Calling Keywords - Hierarchical Structure
description: Learn how keywords can call other keywords to build hierarchical test structure.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, here's the power move: keywords can call OTHER keywords. Build complex operations from simple building blocks!"
story.context: Hierarchical keywords create layers of abstraction. High-level keywords call lower-level keywords, making tests extremely readable.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Brilliant! Your test reads like plain English, but underneath it's a complex choreography of keyword calls!"

instructions: Create test 'Full System Boot' that calls just ONE keyword: Perform Complete Boot Sequence
Create high-level keyword 'Perform Complete Boot Sequence' with [Documentation]: Executes full boot sequence with all checks
Inside it, call three other keywords in order: Initialize Core Systems, Run System Diagnostics, Verify Boot Success
Create keyword 'Initialize Core Systems' that logs: 'Core systems initialized'
Create keyword 'Run System Diagnostics' that logs: 'Diagnostics complete'
Create keyword 'Verify Boot Success' that logs: 'Boot successful'
Note: One test calls one keyword, which calls three keywords - layered abstraction!
hints: Keywords can call other keywords just like tests do
This creates readable, maintainable test hierarchies
solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Full System Boot
    Perform Complete Boot Sequence

*** Keywords ***
Perform Complete Boot Sequence
    [Documentation]    Executes full boot sequence with all checks
    Initialize Core Systems
    Run System Diagnostics
    Verify Boot Success

Initialize Core Systems
    Log    Core systems initialized

Run System Diagnostics
    Log    Diagnostics complete

Verify Boot Success
    Log    Boot successful

theory.title: Exercise 2.2.6: Keywords Calling Keywords
theory.content:
🏗️ Building with Blocks

MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, the ultimate power: keywords calling keywords! It's like building with LEGO - simple blocks combine into complex structures."

"A test calls 'Complete Boot Sequence'. That keyword calls 'Initialize', 'Diagnose', 'Verify'. Each of THOSE could call even more keywords!"

🔺 What is Hierarchical Structure?

Keywords Calling Keywords - Building complex operations from simpler ones

  • ✅ Abstraction layers - Hide complexity behind simple names
  • ✅ Readability - Tests read like business requirements
  • ✅ Reusability - Low-level keywords used by many high-level ones
  • ✅ Maintainability - Change implementation without touching tests

Example Hierarchy:

Test: Complete User Journey
  ↓ calls
Keyword: Register And Login
  ↓ calls
  - Open Application
  - Create Account
  - Login With Credentials
    ↓ calls
    - Enter Username
    - Enter Password
    - Click Login Button

📝 Hierarchical Keywords Example

*** Test Cases ***
E-Commerce Test
    Complete Purchase Flow

*** Keywords ***
Complete Purchase Flow
    [Documentation]    High-level business workflow
    Login As Customer
    Add Items To Cart
    Proceed To Checkout
    Complete Payment

Login As Customer
    Open Browser    ${URL}
    Enter Credentials
    Click Login

Add Items To Cart
    Search For Product    laptop
    Add To Cart
    Search For Product    mouse
    Add To Cart

📋 Hierarchical Keyword Best Practices

  • 🔹 Test level: High-level business keywords only
  • 🔹 High-level keywords: Orchestrate workflows
  • 🔹 Mid-level keywords: Feature-specific actions
  • 🔹 Low-level keywords: Detailed implementations
  • 🔹 Naming: Higher level = more business language

🎯 Your Task

Create a hierarchy: Test calls one keyword, that keyword calls three others. See how clean and readable it becomes!
